model.title: Officer John Barnes and Chief Michael Ansbro Public Safety Officers' Benefit Program Expansion Act of 2026

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Passed Senate):

blocks.text: Officer John Barnes and Chief Michael Ansbro Public Safety Officers' Benefit Program Expansion Act of 2026

This bill establishes processing timelines and expands claims assistance, outreach, and reporting requirements pertaining to claims for benefits under the Public Safety Officers' Benefits (PSOB) program. The PSOB program provides death, disability, and education benefits to public safety officers who are killed or injured in the line of duty and their survivors.

This bill requires the Department of Justice's Bureau of Justice Assistance (BJA) to notify a claimant of any missing information required to process a claim within 90 days of receiving the claim and generally requires the BJA to determine eligibility within 270 days of a completed claim.

In addition, the bill requires the BJA to use its subpoena authority to obtain information or documentation that is necessary to adjudicate a claim if a public agency fails to provide it 30 days after a request.

Under the bill, the BJA must conduct ongoing outreach to promote awareness of the PSOB program. The BJA must also report on whether a delay in processing a claim was due to the inaction of the claimant or the public agency from which information is required.

The bill requires the BJA to implement the recommendations of the Government Accountability Office (GAO) in the 2024 report, Public Safety Officers' Benefits Program: Transparency, Claims Assistance, and Program Management Improvements Needed.
Finally, the GAO must conduct an annual audit of PSOB claims that have been pending for more than one year.

The Officer John Barnes and Chief Michael Ansbro Public Safety Officers' Benefit Program Expansion Act of 2026 aims to speed up and improve the handling of claims under the Public Safety Officers' Benefits (PSOB) program. That program provides death, disability, and education benefits to public safety officers who are killed or hurt in the line of duty, and to their families.

Under the bill, the Department of Justice's Bureau of Justice Assistance (BJA) must tell a claimant within 90 days of receiving a claim if any information needed to process it is missing. The BJA generally must decide whether a claim is eligible within 270 days of receiving a completed claim.
If a public agency does not provide information or documents needed to decide a claim within 30 days of a request, the BJA must use its subpoena power to get them.

The BJA must also keep up ongoing outreach to make more people aware of the PSOB program. It must report on whether any delay in processing a claim was caused by the claimant or by the public agency that had to supply information.

The bill further requires the BJA to carry out the recommendations in a 2024 Government Accountability Office (GAO) report on the program's transparency, claims assistance, and management. Finally, the GAO must audit each year any PSOB claims that have been pending for more than one year.
